payload.outcome: Resolved in PR #2520, in the 'add the newer entry' direction rather than the 'remove the older entry' direction the row suggested. Both snapshots were already listed in .prettierignore; the residual defect was that the newer entry justified itself by claiming parity with the older one. Measured: data/outstanding-issues-snapshot.json genuinely fails prettier --check, so its entry is load-bearing and removing it would cause exactly the regeneration churn it prevents; data/repo-awareness-snapshot.json passes today, so its entry is forward-looking insurance. Its comment now names the real mechanism - the generator writes JSON.stringify(_, null, 2), which always expands arrays, and the two agree only because every array in that schema holds multi-field objects, which Prettier never collapses.
